findings.title: Every tool card shows the same wrench placeholder instead of the tool
findings.description: All ten thumbnails on find are an identical wrench line glyph on a pale-green tile, at every width and theme. The thumbnail slot is the largest visual element on each card but carries no information, and it is the most visible sign of unfinish on the first viewport.
findings.impact: Members who know the tool by sight ('the drill with two batteries') may have to read every title to tell items apart; the page is likely to read as unfinished to first-time members.

evidence.detail: ten identical tiles at x=113 and x=665

findings.recommendation: Decide what the slot is for: real photographs of the library's own stock, or remove the slot and let title and badge carry the card. Do not keep a stand-in.

findings.title: Identity is only the library name in body-size bold text
findings.description: The masthead is a small generic wrench icon and 'Fernhill Tool Library' in bold at body size; no element on any surface comes from the library's world (the membership card, the room, the desk, the stock). DESIGN.md names 'the green of the library's membership card', but nothing on screen lets a member recognise it as such.
findings.impact: 'Neighbourly' lives only in the copy; members are likely to see a generic booking app rather than their volunteer-run library, weakening trust that the reservation reaches real people.
findings.recommendation: Decide which material from the library's own world sets the identity floor on every surface (the name as a mark, the card, the place) and carry it through; keep structure conventional.

findings.title: Search moves below the entire tool list on phones
findings.description: At 375 and 320 the 'Search tools' field, Search button and filter button appear after all ten cards, roughly 1,600px down, while at 1280 they sit above the list.
findings.impact: Mostly-phone members with a tool in mind may scroll the whole list before finding search; the order also differs between desktop and phone.

evidence.detail: detector: Focus order jumps back 'Electric wet tile saw' -> 'Search tools'

findings.recommendation: Keep the search and filter above the list at every width.

findings.title: Tool titles truncate at narrow widths, hiding what distinguishes them
findings.description: Card titles are cut with an ellipsis at 375 and 320: both drills read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...', and 'Extension ladder 3 m ...', 'Hedge trimmer, cord...' lose their size or power detail.
findings.impact: Members may open the wrong drill; 'two batteries' versus 'one battery' is exactly the distinction members use in their own words.
findings.recommendation: Let titles wrap; decide the card layout at narrow widths so the full name fits.

findings.title: Find page overflows horizontally at 320 px
findings.description: At 320 the capture is 346px wide; cards and their right borders extend past the viewport and body text sits closer than 16px to the edge.
findings.impact: Members using larger text or small phones may have to scroll sideways to read deposits and availability.

evidence.detail: LAY-04 Horizontal page overflow; A11Y-05 no reflow at 320

findings.recommendation: Make the card grid and thumbnail shrink to the viewport at 320.

findings.title: Tool detail lists use two different label column widths
findings.description: Under 'Details', Category/Deposit/Available from values start at x≈224, while Chuck/Batteries/Weight/Case values start at x≈180, so one list reads as two misaligned tables.
findings.impact: Members comparing specs may scan a broken column; it undercuts 'careful' on the page where members decide what to borrow.
findings.recommendation: Use one label column for all details of a tool.

findings.title: Reserve bar covers the calendar and pins its button to the viewport edge
findings.description: The fixed white action bar sits across the pick-up calendar (rows 11-17 hidden at 1280; hint and title hidden at 375). At 1280 its button is 16px from the right viewport edge, outside the 1120px content column; in the added state the toast also sits over the weekday header.
findings.impact: Members may not see or reach the session days hidden behind the bar; the primary action floats away from the content it confirms.

evidence.detail: Overlapping text: #reserve; Focused element hidden behind div.actionbar (corroborates)

findings.recommendation: Decide how the bar reserves space for itself so nothing it covers is unreachable, and align the action with the content column at wide widths.

findings.title: Basket session cards form an orphan row with cramped wraps
findings.description: At 1280 the session radios render as one full-width card (Wednesday 28 October) followed by a row of five narrow cards whose labels wrap over three lines; sessions are listed latest first.
findings.impact: The lone card looks like a recommended or different option, and the cramped wraps slow reading of the date and time; latest-first order may lead members to pick the wrong week.
findings.recommendation: Decide one layout for the session list that gives every session the same weight and reads in date order.

findings.title: Available badge loses its fill and contrast in dark mode
findings.description: In dark, 'Available from Sat 10 Oct' renders as dim green text (#2f7d4a on #1d2622) with no pill, while the not-yet-available badges keep a grey pill, so the positive state looks weaker than the negative one.
findings.impact: Members, many in dark mode on phones, may misread which tools can be collected soonest.

evidence.detail: A11Y-11 Text contrast below 4.5:1 fg #2f7d4a on bg #1d2622 (corroborates)

findings.recommendation: Compose the available badge for dark with the declared dark selection and success roles.

findings.title: Filters panel uses unthemed browser-default date and select controls
findings.description: The filters panel shows a native 'yyyy/mm/dd' date input with the system calendar glyph and a native select; the 'Category' label sits about 30px lower than 'Available from', so the two fields do not align.
findings.impact: The yyyy/mm/dd pattern conflicts with the en-GB 'Saturday 17 October' format used everywhere else and may confuse members; the panel reads as unfinished.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether the filter reuses the pick-up calendar's session days; align the two fields on one baseline.

findings.title: Wide layouts leave the right half empty and footer bands stop short
findings.description: At 1280 the tool, confirm and done pages put text, inputs and the 'What happens next' card in a ~610px column while summary cards span 1088px, leaving a large empty right half; on basket and done the white footer ends mid-viewport with bare grey below.
findings.impact: Lunch-break desktop members are likely to see the flow as unfinished; the mixed widths weaken grouping between summary and form.
findings.recommendation: Decide one content width per page type and let the page ground or footer fill the viewport.

findings.title: Done page has no focal point marking the reservation, and the basket count persists
findings.description: 'Reservation confirmed' is a plain H1 above a definition list; the reservation number is in body text in the list; the nav still reads 'Basket (1)'.
findings.impact: Members may not be sure the reservation went through or which number to quote at the desk; 'Basket (1)' suggests the tool is still unreserved.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the member must carry away (number, session, what to bring) and give it the page's emphasis; clear the basket count after confirming.

strengths: One filled button per page, always the job's action (Search, Reserve this tool, Continue, Confirm reservation).
Copy in the desk volunteer's voice with concrete details: deposits on every card, specs, 'Nothing is paid online', phone number in the footer.
Dark theme composed rather than inverted (cards lighter than ground, mint primary, readable error summary at 375).
keep: Keep the plain, concrete volunteer voice and the single-primary-action discipline; add identity and finish around them rather than more controls.
not_assessable: Toast fade and button colour transitions, select open state, hover/focus styling, keyboard reachability (detectors report issues; behavioural).
notes: Subagent isolation. Read only the packet, role instructions, design-panel.md, brand-expression.md and, after unsealing, the anti-slop rule list. No baseline/ folder: pairwise not applicable. Detector output was opened only after critic-1.verdict.json was written. One early Bash call was denied; screens were enumerated with Grep instead.
